title: Cap Blasting Non-Electric M7
description: NOTICE OF PROPOSED PROCUREMENT Canada has a requirement for the item detailed below: GSIN: N1375 – Demolition Materials UNSPSC: 46101600 –Ammunition Description: Cap Blasting Non-Electric M7 A requirement exists to resupply Canada with the Cap Blasting Non-Electric M7. The Cap Blasting Non-Electric M7 is required as the first step of an explosive shockwave in an explosive train when using a non-electric method of initiation. It is functioned by inserting an igniferous burning fuse into the open end and being crimped onto the burning fuse. When the flame from the burning fuse exits the end of the fuse, it ignites a primary explosive composition which in turn transfers a shockwave into the secondary explosive component in the Cap Blasting Non-Electric M7. The Cap Blasting Non-Electric M7 is primarily used in military applications for demolition purposes. Quantity: 3,000 units - Delivery to Canadian Forces Ammunition Depot (CFAD) Dundurn, Dundurn, Saskatchewan on or before 01 November 2027. 3,500 units - Delivery to Canadian Forces Ammunition Depot (CFAD) Angus, Angus, Ontario on or before 01 November 2027. 3,000 units - Delivery to Canadian Forces Ammunition Depot (CFAD) Dundurn, Dundurn, Saskatchewan between 01 September 2028 and 30 November 2028. 3,500 units - Delivery to Canadian Forces Ammunition Depot (CFAD) Angus, Angus, Ontario between 01 September 2028 and 30 November 2028. Unit of Issue: Each, per unit 1. Security Requirements There are no security requirements associated with this procurement. 2. Controlled Goods This procurement is subject to the Controlled Goods Program. 3. The Crown retains the right to negotiate with suppliers on any procurement. 4. Documents may be submitted in either official language of Canada. 5. title: Germany – Installation of fitted kitchens – Küchentechnik
description: Auf dem innerstädtischen Grundstück der Königsegg-Grundschule in Immenstadt wird die bestehende Sporthalle zurückgebaut und durch einen Ersatzneubau mit Sporthalle, Verwaltung für Schule und Hort, Kinderhort und Mensa ersetzt. Die beengte innerstädtische Lage erfordert eine kompakte Lösung am Standort der bisherigen Halle. Im Neubau entstehen eine Einfeldsporthalle mit Nebenräumen im Untergeschoss, Verwaltungsräume für Schule und Hort im Erdgeschoss sowie ein zweigeschossiger Hortbereich für ca. 250 Kinder in den beiden Obergeschossen. Eine Mensa mit Küche für ca. 105 Kinder befindet sich ebenfalls im 2. OG. Die Nutzung erfolgt durch Grundschule, Hort und Ganztagsklassen. Die Anbindung an den Bestand erfolgt barrierefrei mit einem neuen Aufzug im Neubau. Begleitende Umbauten im Schulgebäude ermöglichen die Umnutzung bestehender Horträume für Ganztagsklassen. Die Fachräume im UG-Bestand bleiben erhalten und stehen ebenfalls auch dem Hort zur Verfügung. Der Neubau wird in Massiv- und Holzbauweise errichtet. Die Sporthalle und das EG bestehen aus Stahlbeton, die Obergeschosse aus Holzrahmen- und Holztafelbau. Das Dach ist als versetztes Pultdach mit Gründach und Blechdeckung ausgeführt. Die Fassade kombiniert Faserzementplatten und Holzverkleidung. Die Außenanlagen werden neu strukturiert. Es entstehen eingefriedete Freiflächen für Schule und Hort, sowie ein neuer Allwetterplatz. Ausgeschrieben wird diese Maßnahme in Einzelgewerken.

description: Allgemein: Im Bauabschnitt 1 werden die Freiflächen zwischen Ostflügel des Schlosses und der Ilmböschung bearbeitet. Das Bearbeitungsgebiet reicht von der nördlichen Gebäudekante des Schlosses bis an die Sternbrücke und schließt dabei die Fläche zwischen dem Osteingang des Schlosses und der Sternbrücke mit ein. Die z.Zt. in Bau befindliche Ilmterrasse schließt unmittelbar an das Bearbeitungsgebiet an. Der nördliche Teilbereich wird mit Wassergebundener Wegedecke befestigt und mit inselartigen Strauch-/Staudenpflanzungen versehen. Die Fläche zwischen Osteingang Schloss und Sternbrücke erhält einen Natursteinpflasterbelag. Alle Erdarbeiten werden durch das TLDA/ Archäologische Denkmalpflege begleitet. title: Architect and Engineering Services
description: This solicitation will be designated as a 100% Small Business set aside. A single award acquisition will be made. The awardee must be Small Business certified at time of award. This procurement is conducted under Far subpart 36.102, which requires A-E contracts to be negotiated on the basis of demonstrated competence and qualifications for the required professional services. A Standard Form (SF) 330 will be required. This project includes Design Phase architecture and engineering (A&E) services for Project AFBCIF# 270022 (Project #ZQEL 25-0004), Repair Club Kitchen and Dining Room at Youngstown ARS. Scope of work includes technical engineering specifications, structural drawings, and floor layouts through 35%, 65%, and 100% design completion marks. The project site is located at the 910 Airlift Wing (AFRC), Youngstown Air Reserve Station, 3976 King Graves Rd, Vienna OH 44473-5931 (Trumbull County). The magnitude of this project is between $100,000 and $250,000. Total contract performance period is 120 calendar days from the date of receipt of the notice to proceed. The award will be a Firm-Fixed Price contract. The NAICS Code is 541310; the Size Standard is $12.5 million average annual receipts over the past three years. Paper copies of the solicitation will not be provided as these documents, which include the solicitation and specifications, can be downloaded from https://sam.gov and should be available on or about 24 September 2026. As this is a federal construction project, the Construction Wage Rate Requirement applies. Once the solicitation is posted, it is incumbent upon the interested parties to review this posting frequently for any updates, changes, and/or amendments to any and all documents. The closing date for submission of offers is estimated to be on or about 22 October 2026 at 10:00am EDT and will be contained in the solicitation package. Interested parties should identify themselves by registering on the Interested Vendors List (IVL) found on the sam.gov website. Contractors are advised that in order to receive an award as the prime contractor, they must be listed and active in the System for Award Management (SAM) database for the NAICS code 541310. Failure to register will disqualify a contractor from award should the contractor be selected, not registered, nor active at the time of submission. Contractors may register via the Internet SAM website at https://sam.gov. Recommend registering immediately in order to be eligible for timely award. Contractors are also advised that they must complete the Online Representations and Certifications Application or risk having their proposals declared non-responsive. All responsible sources may submit a SF 330 which shall be considered by the Air Force Reserves. The dates cited above are estimates, not actual.

title: ARSOF Training Support Services
description: THIS IS NOT A NOTICE OF SOLICITATION ISSUANCE, BUT RATHER A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) from industry that will allow the Government to identify interested sources capable of meeting the requirement. The information sought is for planning purposes only and shall not be construed as a request for quote (RFQ), request for proposal (RFP), invitation for bid (IFB), or as an obligation or commitment on the part of the Government to acquire any product or service. There shall be no basis for claims against the Government as a result of information submitted in response to the RFI. The Government does not intend to award a contract on the basis of this RFI or otherwise pay for any information submitted by respondents to this request. This notice is for market research purposes only and is not indicative of a full requirement. Should a requirement arise, the full requirement will be detailed in the solicitation. See the attached Draft Performance Work Statement (PWS). The anticipated period of performance will be for a 12-month base period and four (4) 12-month option periods. The anticipated base period includes a 30-day phase-in. The anticipated NAICS code is 611710 �Educational Support Services� with a size standard of $24 million dollars. Documentation provided must address all required elements listed. Contractors interested in providing these services must be registered in the System for Award Management (www.sam.gov). Providing only a reference to a website is unacceptable for purposes of this announcement and will not be considered. All proprietary or corporate data received shall be clearly identified and will be protected from release to sources outside the Government. Do NOT submit classified material. Contractors responding to this RFI are asked to provide the following information: 1. Company�s full name and address, and Point of Contact information 2. Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) 3. Business size (whether large, small, small-disadvantaged, 8(a), HUB Zone, women-owned, Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business, historically black college or university, and/or minority service institute). - Please also advise the Government of pending changes in the business size status, if applicable. 4. Facility Clearance Level (FCL) 5. CMMC Unique Identifier (UID) 6. A brief Statement of Capability (no more than 10 pages); which responds to the following question and demonstrates the ability to meet the requirements specified in the Draft PWS. - Question 1: What is your company�s experience providing training support services to Special Operations Forces (SOF) elements across the Department of War (DoW) or other federal agencies? - Question 2: What is your company�s recruitment and retention strategy as it relates to SOF specialized instructors, role-players, and training support personnel? - Question 3: What is your company�s experience with similarly sized contracts? Briefly describe your contract management strategy. - Notice: Please consider providing potential pricing data on Attachment 1- ROM. This will be used for Market Research purposes and will not be considered a Quote or Proposal. Pricing submitted on the ROM is non-binding. Email responses to Maegan Castro at maegan.n.castro.civ@socom.mil and Justin Burke at justin.burke@socom.mil. Reference �Sources Sought � ARSOF RFI� in the subject line. No requests for capability briefings will be honored as a result of this notice. Information provided will not be used as a part of any subsequent solicitation requirement. Interested sources who submit data are responsible for appropriately marking information if it is proprietary in nature. No feedback will be provided regarding individual capability statements. No reimbursements will be made for any costs associated with providing information in response to this announcement and/or any follow-up information requests. Failure to respond to this RFI does not preclude participation in any future associated requests for quotations that may be issued. However, any potential small business set-asides will be based upon the feedback received. Respondents will NOT be individually notified of the results. However, if the final determination results in the verification of a sole-source negotiation, a Notice of Intent to Sole Source and the redacted Justification and Approval will be posted to www.sam.gov. For information regarding this notice, contact Maegan Castro at the email address listed above. Respondents are cautioned that due to file size limitation and email security protocols, there is a risk that not all correspondence will be received by this office. It is the interested parties� responsibility to ensure receipt of all email correspondence. If receipt has not be acknowledged within 24 hours, please contact the Contracting Office at 910-432-7688.

title: B--GUSG HABITAT HYDRO-LOGIC RESTORATION 202
description: GUSG HABITAT HYDRO-LOGIC RESTORATION 2026 AMENDMENT 1 09/10/2026- This amendment is to reopen and extend the due date to 09/14/2026 12pm (noon) MD. This is a construction contract to treat habitat for Gunnison sage-grouse, a species listed as endangered under the Endangered Species Act (ESA). The goal of this project is to improve drainage on rural roads on government lands in the Crawford, Colorado area by installing efficient drainage features that effectively transport surface water off of roadways and onto adjacent sagebrush vegetation, effectively rewatering the landscape in a way that mimics natural hydrologic flow. The government shall not exercise any supervision or control over the contract service providers performing the services herein. Such contract service providers shall be accountable solely to the Contractor who, in turn is responsible to the government.

title: Q999--GCH Technologies - Vanity Short Codes Annual Lease
description: This intent to sole source announcement is posted in accordance with FAR 5.2 Synopses of Proposed Contract Actions. Objective The Department of Veterans Affairs, VISN 05, VACO VA Central Office, Veterans Crisis Line (VCL) requires exclusive leasing, management, and maintenance of SMS vanity short codes 838255 ( VETALK ) and 98801 ( 988, press 1 ) to support 24/7/365 crisis text messaging services. These short codes are mission-critical assets that ensure immediate, reliable access to crisis intervention resources. The contemplated period of performance is 12/22/2026 through 12/21/2027 (Base + four option years) Unique Qualifications GCH Technologies Inc. is the only known responsible source capable of fulfilling these requirements. Supporting justification from the Single Source Justification (P03) includes: GCH Technologies holds exclusive control and carrier-level ownership of short codes 838255 and 98801. Vanity short codes cannot be reassigned without the current owner s cooperation. Replacement of these codes would require full public rebranding, disrupt routing infrastructure, and pose unacceptable risks to continuity of crisis services and public safety. Technical research confirms no other vendor can legally or technically provide these exact short codes. Award Information The incumbent contractor shall be provided with the opportunity to present a quote that shall be accepted as a firm fixed price agreement at the lowest price technically acceptable (LPTA). The Government anticipates the Independent Cost Estimate shall be developed and comparable with the current Contract No. 36C24525P0022 to justify fair and reasonable pricing. The period of performance shall be for one base year period, not to exceed 12-months. The Period of Performance reads as follows: 12/22/2026-12/21/2027 If anyone requests additional information or would like to obtain a copy of the statement of work (SOW) for more details Cassie (KC) White cassie.white@va.gov

title: France – Construction work – Construction de 57 logements sociaux et 118 places de stationnement en sous-sol et 4 places de parking en extérieur. « Les prairies du Jura Lot A1 et Le lynx Boréal lot A2 » ZAC du DESSOUS - SERGY (01)
description: Le projet se décompose de la manière suivante : Un îlot A1 composé de 2 bâtiments A11 et A12. Les bâtiments de l'ilot A1 accueillent 27 logements en accession sociale (PSLA). Les logements proposés vont du T2 au T5 duplex et possèdent tous un balcon ou une terrasse. Certains logements en RDC possèdent aussi des jardins privatifs. Le bâtiment A12 est scindé en deux volumes liés par des passerelles et est en R+2+Combles. Le bâtiment A11 est en R+1+Comble. Le local vélo en RDC est situé en limite de propriété. L'accès piéton à l'ilot A1 s'effectue via l'espace public par une rampe partagée avec les véhicules. Un parking de 4 places (dont une place PMR) se trouve au cœur de l'ilot A1. Un parking, mutualisé entre l'ilot A1 et l'ilot A2, de 118 places se trouve en sous-sol. L'entrée du parking se situe sur l'îlot A1, en limite avec l'îlot A2. Un îlot A2 composé de 3 bâtiments : les bâtiments A21, A22 et A23. Les bâtiments de l'ilot A2 se composent de 30 logements locatifs sociaux. Les logements proposés vont du T2 au T5 duplex et possèdent tous un balcon ou une terrasse. Certains logements en RDC possèdent aussi des jardins privatifs. Le bâtiment A23 est scindé en deux volumes liés par des passerelles et est en R+2+Combles Une crèche et deux locaux associatifs seront livrés brut au RDC du bâtiment A23. Dans le cadre du présent marché, l’attention de l’ENTREPRENEUR est attirée sur le fait que l’opération vise une labellisation RE2020 pour les 2 îlots, ainsi qu’une certification NF Habitat HQE, uniquement pour l’îlot A1.

title: Bitterroot Front 10 Year G-Z IRSC
description: 10/9/2026- Amendment 002 Posted. This Amendment provides responses to additional questions received and corrected solicitation documents. Past Performance evaluation criteria has been amended in the Solicitation to align with requested information in the instructions. Corrected documents are indicated with A002 in the file name with all changes indicated in red text. 9/17/2026- Amendment 001 Posted 8/3/2026- Replaces word versions of Attachements C04c_2a, C04d_3a and C04e_4a (Appendicies A-C) with PDFs. No other corrections. This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with the format in FAR Part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Proposals are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation number 12363N26R4014 is issued as a Request for Proposal (RFP) for the Bitterroot Front G-Z Long Term Integrated Resource Service Contract. The Bitterroot Front Project area spans roughly 145,000 acres across the Stevensville and Darby Ranger Districts, where dense, overstocked mixed?conifer stands and widespread tree mortality have increased susceptibility to insect outbreaks and extreme wildfire behavior. Following a decade of severe fires, the project aims to reduce wildfire risk to nearby communities and restore forest health through treatments such as thinning, harvesting, mechanical fuel reduction, and prescribed burning. These efforts focus on improving stand vigor, promoting fire?adapted species, reducing hazardous fuels, and enhancing safety and effectiveness for wildfire responders. A secondary objective of the long?term contract is to provide a consistent timber supply for local forest products industries, while contractors complete tasks including unit layout, timber cruising, road work, and timber removal as part of a broader strategy to increase the pace and scale of forest restoration. This acquisition is set-aside for small business concerns. The applicable North American Industry Classification Standard Code is 113310 and the small business size standard is 500 Employees This acquisition is a Total Small Business Set-Aside. All responsible sources may submit a quotation which will be considered by the agency. Proposals are to be submitted via email to Mark Phillipp at mark.phillipp@usda.gov and Matt Daigle at matthew.daigle@usda.gov.

description: 14 Oct 2026 Amendment FA301626R00350001 This Amendment is to extend the Proposal due date from 15th October 2026 to 22nd October 2026 at 10AM CDT. A second amendment to the solicitation will follow once complete. If your company already submitted a proposal, please note this update. __________________________________________________________________________ This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products or commercial services prepared in accordance with part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Offers are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation number FA301626R0035 is issued as a Request for Proposal (RFP) to Troubleshoot, Repair and Restore Portable Chillers located at Joint Base San Antonio (JBSA) Fort Sam Houston and Lackland, TX. This acquisition is set-aside for small business concerns. This solicitation incorporates provisions and clauses by reference. The full text of provisions and clauses may be accessed electronically at www.acquisition.gov. Project Overview. This is a service requirement to troubleshoot, repair, and restore eight (8) portable chiller units located at 1555 Gott Street, JBSA Lackland, TX and 2199 Storage Street, JBSA Fort Sam Houston, TX. The Lackland units are currently operating at approximately 50% capacity, while the two units at Fort Sam Houston are non?operational and are not connected to any facility. The contractor shall perform full diagnostics, leak detection, component replacement, and post?repair performance validation to return all units to manufacturer specifications. Work shall encompass comprehensive system diagnostics, pressure and leak detection, targeted component replacement, and post-repair performance validation. Project Scope. The contractor shall provide all labor, materials, tools, transportation, and technical expertise necessary to diagnose, repair, and test all portable chillers and restore them to full operational capability in accordance with manufacturer specifications. Notice to Offeror(s)/Supplier(s): Funds are not presently available for this effort. No award will be made under this solicitation until funds are available. The Government reserves the right to cancel this solicitation, either before or after the closing date. In the event the Government cancels this solicitation, the Government has no obligation to reimburse a firm for any costs. Instructions: Offerors are required to review the solicitation and all associated attachments in their entirety. No other corrections. This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with the format in FAR Part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Proposals are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation number 12363N26R4014 is issued as a Request for Proposal (RFP) for the Bitterroot Front G-Z Long Term Integrated Resource Service Contract. The Bitterroot Front Project area spans roughly 145,000 acres across the Stevensville and Darby Ranger Districts, where dense, overstocked mixed?conifer stands and widespread tree mortality have increased susceptibility to insect outbreaks and extreme wildfire behavior. Following a decade of severe fires, the project aims to reduce wildfire risk to nearby communities and restore forest health through treatments such as thinning, harvesting, mechanical fuel reduction, and prescribed burning. These efforts focus on improving stand vigor, promoting fire?adapted species, reducing hazardous fuels, and enhancing safety and effectiveness for wildfire responders. A secondary objective of the long?term contract is to provide a consistent timber supply for local forest products industries, while contractors complete tasks including unit layout, timber cruising, road work, and timber removal as part of a broader strategy to increase the pace and scale of forest restoration. This acquisition is set-aside for small business concerns. The applicable North American Industry Classification Standard Code is 113310 and the small business size standard is 500 Employees This acquisition is a Total Small Business Set-Aside. All responsible sources may submit a quotation which will be considered by the agency. Proposals are to be submitted via email to Mark Phillipp at mark.phillipp@usda.gov and Matt Daigle at matthew.daigle@usda.gov.

Solicitation number FA301626R0035 is issued as a Request for Proposal (RFP) to Troubleshoot, Repair and Restore Portable Chillers located at Joint Base San Antonio (JBSA) Fort Sam Houston and Lackland, TX. This acquisition is set-aside for small business concerns. This solicitation incorporates provisions and clauses by reference. The full text of provisions and clauses may be accessed electronically at www.acquisition.gov. Project Overview. This is a service requirement to troubleshoot, repair, and restore eight (8) portable chiller units located at 1555 Gott Street, JBSA Lackland, TX and 2199 Storage Street, JBSA Fort Sam Houston, TX. The Lackland units are currently operating at approximately 50% capacity, while the two units at Fort Sam Houston are non?operational and are not connected to any facility. The contractor shall perform full diagnostics, leak detection, component replacement, and post?repair performance validation to return all units to manufacturer specifications. Work shall encompass comprehensive system diagnostics, pressure and leak detection, targeted component replacement, and post-repair performance validation. Project Scope. The contractor shall provide all labor, materials, tools, transportation, and technical expertise necessary to diagnose, repair, and test all portable chillers and restore them to full operational capability in accordance with manufacturer specifications. title: Lead Hazardous Waste Removal for RCMP Indoor Firing Ranges (IFR), Alberta
description: This requirement is for the Royal Canadian Mounted Police. This requirement is open only to those Supply Arrangement Holders under EW479-162880 who can perform the services in the geographical location of Alberta. The requirement is intended to result in the award of one (1) contract. The following Supply Arrangement Holders have been invited to submit a proposal: Stericycle Aevitas Clean Harbors Canada Inc. and Affiliated Companies GFL Environmental Inc. KBL Environmental Ltd. Shield Specialize Emergency Services Inc. Veolia es Canada Services Industriels Inc. Miller Environmental SUMAS Environmental Services Quest Disposal & Recycling Environmental 360 Solutions Description of the Requirement: Lead Hazardous Waste Removal for RCMP Indoor Firing Ranges (IFR), Alberta The Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP) K Division, Real Property and Asset Management has a requirement for the cleaning, removal, packing, disposal and/or recycling of hazardous waste materials from four RCMP Indoor Firing ranges located in Edmonton, Red Deer, Edson and St. Paul, Alberta. Level of Security Requirement: Resource Minimum Security Level Required: RCMP Facility Access Level 2 with Escort (FA2) Applicable Trade Agreements: Canada Free Trade Agreement (CFTA), Canada-Korea Free Trade Agreement, Canada-Chile Free Trade Agreement, Canada-Columbia Free Trade Agreement, Canada-Honduras Free Trade Agreement, Canada-Panama Free Trade Agreement, Canada-Peru Free Trade Agreement, Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), Canada-United Kingdom Trade Continuity Agreement, Canada-Ukraine Free Trade Agreement, Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP), and World Trade Organization – Agreement on Government Procurement (WTO-AGP) Proposed period of contract: The proposed period of contract shall be for one year from date of contract award inclusive, with the irrevocable option to extend the term of the Contract by up to three additional one year periods under the same conditions. Estimated Level of Effort: The estimated level of effort of the contract, per year and across all 4 locations, will be: 10 times per year : Using steel rod, check the depth of rubber pellets from surface of trap to rigid steps of the bullet trap structure or new lead buildup in the middle of trap and its both corners. Add rubber pellets into bullet trap to maintain 600mm (24 inches) depth. Refill the trap hopper with new rubber pellets. Rake rubber pellets to cover rubber membrane at the back of the trap with rubber pellets. Level rubber berm surface to make proper slope. 5 times per year: Fix, patch, and/or flip rubber curtains if applicable 4 times per year: Replacement of rubber curtains or panels if applicable 4 times per year: Lead mining of the bullet trap system 4 times per year: Deep cleaning of firing range, range walls 1.8m AFF, training gear (e.g., target holders, First Air kit, etc.), all horizontal surfaces, control and gun cleaning rooms, floors, HEPA vacuum inside filter sections of supply and exhaust units 5 times per year: Replacement of pre-filters for exhaust ventilation unit HEPA filters replacement must be coordinated with Project Authority and to be done every 5 years (for Edson, St. Paul, and Red Deer sites), and every 4 years (Edmonton HQ) The estimated level of effort provided is for bid evaluated price determination purposes only. Their inclusion does not represent a commitment by Canada that Canada’s future usage of the services described in the bid solicitation will be consistent with this data. Solicitation Number: M5000-25-2334/A Contracting Authority: Sheena Simonson Phone Number: 306-515-1653 E-Mail: sheena.simonson@rcmp-grc.gc.ca Any supplier that wishes to submit a request to be a Supply Arrangement Holder for hazardous waste disposal services may do so by responding to the Request for Supply Arrangement (RFSA) with the solicitation number EW479-162880 on https://canadabuys.canada.ca/en/tender-opportunities. The RFSA will remain valid until such time as Public Services and Procurement Canada (PSPC) no longer considers it to be advantageous to use it.

Ireland – Social research services – Request for Tenders for the Provision of a Rapid Evidence Assessment in relation to reading for pleasure among children and young people in Ireland with a particular focus on boys and young men
description: The Department of Education and Youth is seeking research services from a suitably qualified contractor/s to conduct a rapid evidence review in relation to reading for pleasure among children and young people in Ireland, with a particular focus on boys and young men. For the purposes of this review, the terms children and young people and boys and young men refer to learners from the early learning and care (ELC) sector through primary and post-primary education. The review should therefore consider evidence relating to attitudes, engagement and participation in reading for pleasure across the continuum of educational provision, including key developmental and educational transition points.

title: Ireland – Social research services – Request for Tender for the provision of a rapid evidence review in relation to confidence in maths among children and young people in Ireland with a particular focus on girls and young women
description: The Department is seeking research services from a suitably qualified contractor(s) to conduct a rapid evidence review in relation to confidence in mathematics among children and young people in Ireland, with a particular focus on girls and young women. For the purposes of this review, the terms children and young people and girls and young women refer to learners from the early learning and care (ELC) sector through primary and post-primary education. The review should therefore consider evidence relating to confidence in mathematics and numeracy, including learners' self-belief, mathematical self-efficacy, attitudes towards mathematics, and willingness to engage with mathematical learning across the continuum of educational provision, including key developmental and educational transition points.

description: FROM: AFLCMC/WISK Special Warfare Contracting Office 1895 Fifth Street Wright Patterson AFB, OH 45433-7200 SUBJECT: Request for Information (RFI) � Next Generation Operational Control System (NGOCS) NOTICE This Sources Sought Synopsis (SSS)/Request for Information (RFI) is issued for informational purposes and market research only; it does not constitute a solicitation. The Government will not reimburse any company or individual for any expenses associated with preparing/submitting information in response to this posting. The information provided may be used by the Government in developing its acquisition strategy, statement of work/statement of objectives, and/or performance specifications. Interested parties are responsible for adequately marking proprietary or competition sensitive information contained within their response as instructed later in this posting. BACKGROUND AND SCOPE The United States (US) Air Force Life Cycle Management Center (AFLCMC), Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance & Special Operations Forces (ISR & SOF) Directorate, Special Warfare (SW) Program Office (AFLCMC/WISN) is conducting market research to identify possible sources capable of providing the NGOCS. CAPABILITY GAP Operators currently lack a lightweight, ruggedized, modular body-worn power, data, and edge-compute architecture capable of providing distributed processing capacity beyond the End User Device (EUD) for concurrent high-demand tactical workloads. Fielded systems rely on aging architecture, proprietary cabling, and limited processing capabilities at the edge. Consequently, the EUD is forced to absorb the entirety of application processing, edge-server hosting, message routing, video data links, and peripheral management. During high-tempo combat operations, this overreliance creates latency, power depletion, and reliability bottlenecks that can jeopardize the mission. INSTRUCTION TO POTENTIAL RESPONDENTS Interested parties who desire to participate in this SSS/RFI are encouraged to submit responses that demonstrate they presently have the technology and qualifications to provide the system described above. Responses shall also include the following information: Respondent Data: Company/Institute Name Address Point of Contact (to include phone number and email address) CAGE Code Web Page URL Pursuant to NAICS Code 541512, Computer Systems Design Services, state whether the company is: Small Business (Yes / No) Self-Certified or Third Party Certified Women-Owned Small Business (Yes / No) Self-Certified or Third Party Certified Economically Disadvantaged Women- Owned Small Business (Yes / No) Self-Certified or Third Party Certified HUBZone Certified (Yes / No) Self-Certified or Third Party Certified Veteran Owned Small Business (Yes / No) Self-Certified or Third Party Certified Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (Yes / No) Self-Certified or Third Party Certified 8(a) Certified (Yes / No) Self-Certified or Third Party Certified SBA Certification Date: SBA Graduation Date: State whether the company is domestically or foreign-owned (if foreign, indicate the country of ownership). If development and/or integration is required to meet the system requirements, the Government also needs an estimate of the development cost based on complexity (for planning purposes only) to include PHS&T, such as warranties, portable storage, special tooling required, and training. Indicate whether the company is currently performing this type of work/whether the capability can be obtained under an existing Government contract. Provide the contract number(s) and Government points of contact accordingly. Indicate whether the company currently provides this type of work as a commercial solution. In this instance, �commercial item� means an item that is of a type customarily used by the general public or non-Governmental entities for purposes other than Governmental purposes. Please indicate if this item has been sold, leased, or licensed to the general public; or has been offered for sale, lease, or license to the general public. Indicate whether all materials used are in compliance with the Buy American Act or Berry Amendment (10 U.S.C. 2533a), as applicable. title: Coburn Gore LPOE Art in Architecture Project
description: Document Added & Updated: 0332CG-AIA- Coburn Gore AIA Questions & Answers V3 Dated 07 October 2026 The U.S. General Services Administration (GSA) Art in Architecture Program commissions American artists (citizens and Lawful Permanent Residents or Permanent Workers of the United States) to create publicly scaled and permanently installed artworks for Federal buildings nationwide. GSA announces an opportunity for a Federal art commission in conjunction with the new construction of the Coburn Gore Land Port of Entry (LPOE) in Coburn, Maine. The new facility will strengthen supply chains, improve operational capabilities and facility infrastructure, spur economic growth, and bolster the country�s security. The project will provide a fully operational LPOE that coordinates with the tra?c ?ow and operations of the Canadian port of entry at Saint-Augustin-de-Woburn Quebec, Port of Entry. The project will provide a new port that allows Customs and Border Protection to more efficiently carry out its agency mission, their operations and interactions with the public. GSA allocates one-half of one percent (0.5%) of the estimated construction costs of new or modernized Federal facilities for art commissions. The art budget for this project is estimated to be between $275,000 to $400,000. One or more artists will be awarded a fixed-price contract for a commission. Artists who wish to be considered for this GSA art commission must submit application materials to GSA by the SAM Contract Opportunity�s Response Date. Artists may also elect to be considered for all future GSA art commissions by submitting application materials to GSA�s National Artist Registry (Registry). Instructions on how to submit application materials and join the Registry are available on the following Web site: https://www.gsa.gov/real-estate/design-and-construction/art-in-architecturefine-arts/art-in-architecture-program/art-in-architecture-national-artist-registry All artists who wish to be considered as candidates for a commission at the LPOE in Coburn Gore, ME must have their application materials submitted and received by GSA by 12:00 PM Eastern Time on 22 October 2026. Artists� submissions received after the deadline will not be considered for this project but will be eligible for consideration on future GSA commissions alongside the other artists on the Registry. Artists already on the Registry need not resubmit but may elect to update their information prior to the deadline. GSA evaluates artists based on the following criteria: the media, materials, content and style of the artist�s past work, along with the artist�s past performance and experience with commissions or projects similar to the one described in this synopsis. Shortlisted artists will be contacted and asked to submit additional information, including a statement that the artist can perform the work associated with the GSA commission within the identified budget. GSA will count the combined weight of all the selection criteria as significantly more important than price. At minimum, the scope of services for this commission will require collaboration with the lead designer selected for the land port of entry project; travel to the project site; development and presentation of preliminary and final concepts; fabrication of the artwork; participation in meetings and conservation reviews as necessary; delivery and installation of the artwork; professional documentation of, and detailed maintenance planning for the artwork at the project site. For informational purposes: Artists selected for the contract award must be Permanent Residents or Citizens of the United States of America. Artists selected for the contract award will be required to have an active registration in the System for Award Management (SAM) at the time of award. Instructions for creating an account and activating registration in SAM may be found at www.sam.gov. Artists selected for the contract award will be required to renew the registration in SAM on an annual basis for the duration of the project. In accordance with Executive Order (EO) 13934, agencies should prioritize the commission of works of art that portray historically significant Americans or events of American historical significance or illustrate the ideals upon which our Nation was founded. Inquiries concerning the project should be directed to the following email address: Molly.Lewis@gsa.gov and reference the synopsis number in the subject line. No questions will be answered after 07 October 2026 12:00pm EST.

title: El Toro Range Improvements
description: THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ONLY. This notice is issued solely for market research and planning purposes to determine the availability and capability of qualified sources under NAICS 236220. The Government is seeking responses from both small and large business concerns. This is not a solicitation, and no contract will be awarded from this notice. Project Overview: The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) is conducting market research for a potential Design-Build requirement supporting improvements to a range in the Irvine, California area. The anticipated scope includes restroom upgrades, erosion control, concrete pad installation, electrical upgrades, and large-scale asphalt pavement repair. The estimated magnitude is between $1,000,000 and $5,000,000. A brief outline of the work is below: Electrical System Upgrade Provide and install a 225?kVA transformer (208Y/120V, 3?phase) and a 600?amp main distribution panel. Erosion Control (25? and 50?Yard Ranges) Conduct geotechnical borings and design a compliant erosion control system (retaining structures, drainage). Construct stabilization measures, install drainage, and provide as?built documentation. Pavement Rehabilitation (~30,000 SY) Assess roadway conditions and drainage patterns. Perform milling, full?depth asphalt repairs, subgrade stabilization, HMA paving, compaction, and final striping. Restroom Renovations Fully renovate two commercial restrooms, including demolition, framing, waterproofing, electrical, plumbing, fixtures, finishes, and accessibility components. Water Pressure Improvements Assess existing domestic water system and design a solution to increase operating pressure to 60�70 psi. Furnish and install all new equipment, controls, piping, and backflow prevention. Range Concrete Improvements (25?Yard Pad & Lane Markings) Survey, grade, and install new concrete pad, walking paths, and reinforced firing lanes. Install or tie into an existing lead?collection system. Provide durable, visible lane markings at the 3, 5, 7, 15, and 25?yard distances Required Capabilities: Respondents should demonstrate experience in design-build construction projects of similar magnitude and complexity, including: restroom renovations, water pressure system installation, slope stabilization/erosion control, concrete pad construction, range marking, electrical upgradess, and asphalt roadway rehabilitation. Submission Requirements: Interested firms should submit a capabilities statement (no more than 10 pages) including but not limited to the following information: � Company name, address, UEI, CAGE code, business size and socioeconomic status. � Bonding capability (single and aggregate). � Relevant project experience within the past 5 years. � Ability to perform work in Southern California. � Availability of personnel capable of meeting FBI security requirements (US Citizens only) � Statement of interest in performing as a prime contractor. Submission Instructions: Responses shall be submitted via email to the following: Amanda Mobley, Contracting Officer � almobley@fbi.gov Disclaimer: This Sources Sought Notice is for informational purposes only and does not constitute a solicitation. No reimbursement will be provided for any costs incurred in preparing a response. The Government has not determined the acquisition strategy and will evaluate capabilities from both small and large business concerns.

title: Coburn Gore LPOE Art in Architecture Project
description: Document Added & Updated: 0332CG-AIA- Coburn Gore AIA Questions & Answers V2 Dated 09 September 2026 The U.S. General Services Administration (GSA) Art in Architecture Program commissions American artists (citizens and Lawful Permanent Residents or Permanent Workers of the United States) to create publicly scaled and permanently installed artworks for Federal buildings nationwide. GSA announces an opportunity for a Federal art commission in conjunction with the new construction of the Coburn Gore Land Port of Entry (LPOE) in Coburn, Maine. The new facility will strengthen supply chains, improve operational capabilities and facility infrastructure, spur economic growth, and bolster the country�s security. The project will provide a fully operational LPOE that coordinates with the tra?c ?ow and operations of the Canadian port of entry at Saint-Augustin-de-Woburn Quebec, Port of Entry. The project will provide a new port that allows Customs and Border Protection to more efficiently carry out its agency mission, their operations and interactions with the public. GSA allocates one-half of one percent (0.5%) of the estimated construction costs of new or modernized Federal facilities for art commissions. The art budget for this project is estimated to be between $275,000 to $400,000. One or more artists will be awarded a fixed-price contract for a commission. Artists who wish to be considered for this GSA art commission must submit application materials to GSA by the SAM Contract Opportunity�s Response Date. Artists may also elect to be considered for all future GSA art commissions by submitting application materials to GSA�s National Artist Registry (Registry). Instructions on how to submit application materials and join the Registry are available on the following Web site: https://www.gsa.gov/real-estate/design-and-construction/art-in-architecturefine-arts/art-in-architecture-program/art-in-architecture-national-artist-registry All artists who wish to be considered as candidates for a commission at the LPOE in Coburn Gore, ME must have their application materials submitted and received by GSA by 12:00 PM Eastern Time on 22 October 2026. Artists� submissions received after the deadline will not be considered for this project but will be eligible for consideration on future GSA commissions alongside the other artists on the Registry. Artists already on the Registry need not resubmit but may elect to update their information prior to the deadline. GSA evaluates artists based on the following criteria: the media, materials, content and style of the artist�s past work, along with the artist�s past performance and experience with commissions or projects similar to the one described in this synopsis. Shortlisted artists will be contacted and asked to submit additional information, including a statement that the artist can perform the work associated with the GSA commission within the identified budget. GSA will count the combined weight of all the selection criteria as significantly more important than price. At minimum, the scope of services for this commission will require collaboration with the lead designer selected for the land port of entry project; travel to the project site; development and presentation of preliminary and final concepts; fabrication of the artwork; participation in meetings and conservation reviews as necessary; delivery and installation of the artwork; professional documentation of, and detailed maintenance planning for the artwork at the project site. For informational purposes: Artists selected for the contract award must be Permanent Residents or Citizens of the United States of America. Artists selected for the contract award will be required to have an active registration in the System for Award Management (SAM) at the time of award. Instructions for creating an account and activating registration in SAM may be found at www.sam.gov. Artists selected for the contract award will be required to renew the registration in SAM on an annual basis for the duration of the project. In accordance with Executive Order (EO) 13934, agencies should prioritize the commission of works of art that portray historically significant Americans or events of American historical significance or illustrate the ideals upon which our Nation was founded. Inquiries concerning the project should be directed to the following email address: Molly.Lewis@gsa.gov and reference the synopsis number in the subject line.

Preliminary Statement of Work DESCRIPTION The Minneapolis Veterans Affairs Health Care System (MVAHCS) has a continued need for Integrated Pest Management Services (IPMS) that are a part of a comprehensive Integrated Pest Management (IPM) program. IPM is a process for achieving long term, environmentally sound pest suppression through the use of a wide variety of technological and management practices. Control strategies in an IPM program extend beyond the application of pesticides to include structural and procedural modifications that reduce the food, water, harborage, and access used by pest. Contractor provided IPMS will be utilized as stated within this Statement of Work. IPMS will be utilized in all grounds and buildings herein the MVAHCS. The Contractor shall provide detailed, site-specific recommendations for structural and procedural modifications to aid in pest prevention. The Contractor must meet the performance expectations of the client in eradicating and suppressing the following pests: Indoor population of rats, mice, wasps, cockroaches, ants, flies, spiders, and any other arthropod or common pest including bed bugs. Pests that are located outside of the specified buildings, but within the property boundaries of the buildings including: raccoons, snakes, woodchucks, turkeys, bees and bee hives, birds etc. Contractor must eradicate bed bug infestations by means of convection heat treatment method.
